resources.name: SoundBetter
resources.description: Spotify-owned marketplace with 50,000+ vetted music professionals across 176 countries. Find session musicians, producers, singers, and engineers by reviews, price, location, and credits. Free to browse and hire; pros set their own rates.
resources.cost: Free to browse; service prices set by pros (~$100–$2,000+). Platform takes ~8% total (5% commission + 3% processing).

resources.name: AirGigs
resources.description: Marketplace for hiring session musicians, vocalists, and audio engineers for remote recording. Launched in 2012, it features detailed artist profiles, audio samples, and secure escrow payments.
resources.cost: Free to browse. Buyers pay 4.7% service fee (minimum $5). Sellers: Top Rated/Featured receive 90% (10% to AirGigs); non-featured receive 85% (15% to AirGigs). Minimum commission $8 per order.
highlights: Tiered commission structure rewards Top Rated sellers

resources.name: Fiverr — Music & Audio
resources.description: Global freelance marketplace with a large Music & Audio category. Find session guitarists, drummers, bassists, vocalists, and more. Filter by instrument, genre, budget, and delivery time.
resources.cost: Services start at ~$5. Average session musician gig: $50–$400. Buyers pay 5.5% service fee + $2 small-order fee on orders under $50.

resources.name: Musiversal
resources.description: Subscription-based platform for live, directed recording sessions with world-class musicians. Collaborate in real time, give feedback instantly, and receive takes within 15 minutes. Raised $6M Series A in September 2025 for US expansion and new services including co-writing, production, and marketing.
resources.cost: Unlimited subscription: $199–$249/mo (verify current pricing on site). 100+ musicians, 1,000+ members, 100,000+ sessions per year.
highlights: All instruments: drums, guitar, bass, keys, strings, horns, vocals
Rapidly expanding with Series A funding

resources.name: Studio Pros
resources.description: Los Angeles-based online studio offering work-for-hire session musicians. Upload your song, get a preview in 48 hours, request revisions, and download final files. You own 100% of the recording. Contact for specific per-track pricing.
resources.cost: Contact for per-track pricing and full production quotes. Video production: $1,099 full music video, $599 lyric video, $99 static frame.

resources.name: Supreme Tracks
resources.description: Curated roster of professional session musicians who record in pro studios. A session producer reviews your demo, translates your vision, and handpicks the right player.
resources.cost: Contact for current pricing details.
highlights: Handpicked musicians matched to your genre

resources.name: BeatStars
resources.description: The largest beat-selling marketplace connecting producers and artists. Browse, preview, and license beats with instant delivery. Supports exclusive and non-exclusive licenses.
resources.cost: Free to browse. Beat prices set by producers (typically $20–$500+). Starter $19.99/year; Growth $79.99/year; Professional $179.88/year. 12% service fee on marketplace sales.
highlights: Largest producer community in the industry
Updated subscription tiers as of September 2024

resources.name: Airbit
resources.description: Beat marketplace focused on producer-friendly pricing. Upload and sell beats with 100% revenue retention on paid plans. Under BandLab ownership since 2023, integrated with 60M+ user base.
resources.cost: Free tier (limited uploads). Platinum $19.99/mo or $7.99/mo annual. 100% revenue retention on paid plans.
highlights: 100% revenue to seller on paid plans

resources.name: SoundBetter — Producers
resources.description: Find and hire music producers through the SoundBetter marketplace. Filter by genre, credits, reviews, and budget. Work directly with the producer through the platform.
resources.cost: Free to browse; producer rates vary (~$200–$5,000+). ~8% platform fee.
highlights: Same trust system as SoundBetter session musicians

resources.name: Splice — Sounds & Samples
resources.description: Massive royalty-free sample library used by 10M+ producers. Access millions of loops, one-shots, presets, and MIDI packs. In-DAW integrations with Pro Tools 2025.6+, Studio One 7+, and Ableton Live 12.3 (beta). Free account access to all free LABS instruments from Spitfire Audio.
resources.cost: Free tier with limited access. Instrument $12.99/mo; Creator $19.99/mo; Creator+ $39.99/mo. Plugin rent-to-own from $9.99/mo.
highlights: Free LABS instruments on free tier

resources.name: Tracklib
resources.description: Legal sample-clearance platform. Browse a catalog of real, original recordings and license samples with pre-cleared rights for your productions. Mobile app launched May 2025. Now includes royalty-free 'Sounds' library alongside licensed 'Songs' library.
resources.cost: Free to browse and preview. Premium and Professional subscription plans with licensing included. Previous per-license pricing (Category A $1,500, B $500, C $50) now incorporated into subscription model.

resources.name: SoundBetter — Mixing Engineers
resources.description: Browse and hire mixing engineers from SoundBetter's vetted roster. Filter by genre specialty, credits, reviews, and budget. Includes Grammy-winning engineers.
resources.cost: Free to browse; rates set by engineers. ~8% platform fee.
highlights: Engineers with major label credits available

resources.name: LANDR
resources.description: AI-powered mastering platform. Upload your track and get an instant master. Includes distribution to streaming platforms, sample packs, mastering plugin, and social platform monetization (Pro+ tier as of mid-2025). Standalone distribution plans also available.
resources.cost: Essentials $12.99/mo (unlimited MP3 masters, unlimited distribution, 100 sample credits); Standard $19.99/mo (3 WAV/mo, standard plugin, 150 credits); Pro $24.99/mo (unlimited MP3+WAV+HD WAV, unlimited distribution, 200 credits). 20–36% discount on annual billing. Distribution standalone from $23.99/year.
highlights: Unlimited free previews before you pay
Includes distribution to Spotify, Apple Music, etc.
Social monetization on Pro tier (updated mid-2025)

resources.name: eMastered
resources.description: AI mastering service co-founded by a Grammy-winning engineer (Smith Carlson, Taylor Swift's 1989). More mastering controls than LANDR — adjust EQ, compression, stereo width, and loudness.
resources.cost: Entry-level: $19/mo annual commitment ($156/year for 12 months). Monthly plans available at higher rates. Includes unlimited high-res WAV downloads.

resources.name: AirGigs — Mixing & Mastering
resources.description: Hire mixing and mastering engineers on the AirGigs marketplace. Compare profiles, listen to before/after samples, and read reviews from other artists.
resources.cost: Service prices set by engineers. Buyers pay 4.7% fee (minimum $5). Sellers receive tiered commission (85–90%).
highlights: Wide price range for all budgets

resources.name: Fiverr — Mixing & Mastering
resources.description: Find mixing and mastering engineers on Fiverr's freelance marketplace. Good for budget-conscious projects with fast turnaround needs.
resources.cost: Services from ~$20. Buyers pay 5.5% service fee + $2 small-order fee on orders under $50.

resources.name: BandLab — Mastering
resources.description: Free AI mastering built into the BandLab platform. Upload your finished mix and get an instant master. Part of a free, cloud-based DAW with 100M+ users. Optional Membership tier for premium AI tools and distribution.
resources.cost: Free (basic AI mastering). Optional Membership tier available for premium features.

resources.name: SoundBetter — Singers & Songwriters
resources.description: Find male and female session singers, topliners, and songwriters on SoundBetter. Filter by genre, vocal range, and budget. Includes background vocalists and topliner writers.
resources.cost: Free to browse; vocalist rates vary (~$100–$2,000+). ~8% platform fee.

resources.name: Vocalizr
resources.description: ⚠️ Platform dedicated to connecting producers with vocalists and topline songwriters. NEW SIGNUPS CURRENTLY CLOSED. Existing users can still log in. Post public or private gigs, run vocal contests, and license ready-made vocals from their marketplace.
resources.cost: Access Pass: $11.99/mo. 3.9% service fee (minimum $3). Note: NEW SIGNUPS ARE SUSPENDED — do not direct new users to sign up until this changes.
highlights: Contest feature for discovering vocal talent

resources.name: Fiverr — Singers & Songwriters
resources.description: Hire session singers, background vocalists, jingle singers, and songwriters on Fiverr. Wide range of genres and pricing. Filter by vocal style, gender, and language.
resources.cost: Services from ~$20. Average vocal track: $50–$200+. Buyers pay 5.5% service fee + $2 fee on orders under $50.
highlights: Huge selection of vocal styles and languages

resources.name: AirGigs — Vocalists
resources.description: Hire session singers, background vocalists, and songwriters on AirGigs. Listen to audio samples, read reviews, and work through secure escrow payments.
resources.cost: Service prices set by vocalists. Buyers pay 4.7% fee (minimum $5). Sellers receive tiered commission (85–90%).

resources.name: Kompoz
resources.description: Online music collaboration platform where producers post projects and vocalists/songwriters contribute their parts asynchronously. Royalty splits built in.
resources.cost: Free to join. Premium+ membership available for private projects and WAV downloads.

resources.name: ProCollabs
resources.description: Online music collaboration platform with a manually verified membership. Share projects, find vocalists and songwriters, and collaborate across borders.
resources.cost: Free to join (manually verified).

resources.name: Vampr
resources.description: The #1 music industry networking app — like LinkedIn for musicians. Swipe-based discovery connects you with musicians, producers, engineers, and industry professionals. Acquired by Vinyl Group in June 2023. All users can now distribute music free to Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer and major DSPs.
resources.cost: Free tier: music distribution available; keep 80% of royalties. Pro: $19.99/3 months or $44.99/year. Pro keeps 100% of royalties.
highlights: Free music distribution for all users
Apple "Best of 2017"; Fast Company Most Innovative
Owned by Vinyl Group since June 2023

resources.name: BandLab
resources.description: Free cloud-based DAW and social music platform with 100M+ users. Create, collaborate with up to 50 people per project, and share music — all from your browser or phone. Acquired Airbit in 2023, expanding its ecosystem.
resources.cost: Free (all core features). Optional Membership tier for AI tools and distribution.
highlights: Free multi-track recording, mixing, and mastering

resources.name: BandMix
resources.description: The largest musician classifieds site for finding local band members, session players, and music industry professionals. Search by location, instrument, genre, and experience level. ⚠️ Note: Multiple BBB complaints and Trustpilot reviews cite aggressive auto-renewal billing practices.
resources.cost: Free account (limited). Premier: $12.95/mo, $33.95/3mo, or $99.95/yr ($8.33/mo).
highlights: Digital Auditions feature contacts 100 relevant musicians
Musician, Band, and Industry account types
⚠️ Verify auto-renewal terms before signing up

resources.name: Soundtrap
resources.description: Spotify-owned cloud DAW built for real-time collaboration. Multiple users can work on the same track simultaneously with video chat. Includes loops, instruments, and podcasting tools. Plan names may have been rebranded; verify current tiers at soundtrap.com.
resources.cost: Free tier available. Premium tiers from $9.99/mo. Soundtrap + Spotify Premium bundle $19.99/mo.
highlights: Real-time simultaneous collaboration with video chat

resources.name: Splice — Community
resources.description: Splice's community hub (via Discord) hosts beat battles, remix contests, and producer networking. 10M+ producers share projects, collaborate on stems, and participate in creative challenges.
resources.cost: Free (Discord community). Splice subscription from $12.99/mo (Instrument) or $19.99/mo (Creator).
highlights: Beat battles with major producers (Murda Beatz, Chromeo)
Cloud project sharing for DAW collaboration

resources.name: ASCAP
resources.description: American Society of Composers, Authors, and Publishers. Non-profit PRO representing 18M+ musical works. Collects performance royalties from radio, TV, live venues, and streaming for songwriters and publishers.
resources.cost: One-time $50 joining fee. No annual dues. Member-owned.
highlights: Airport and hotel discounts for members
Join one PRO only — cannot also be BMI member

resources.name: BMI
resources.description: Broadcast Music, Inc. The largest US PRO with 900,000+ songwriters and 14M+ compositions. Collects and distributes performance royalties for songwriters and publishers.
resources.cost: Free to join as a songwriter. No membership fee.
highlights: Free to join — no fees for songwriters
Songwriting camps and app subscriptions for members
Good first choice for indie songwriters

resources.name: SESAC
resources.description: Selective, invitation-only PRO. Much smaller roster than ASCAP/BMI (30,000+ songwriters, 400,000+ compositions). Focus on high-profile writers in TV, film, and major releases.
resources.cost: Invitation only. No public fee structure.
highlights: Notable members: Adele, Bob Dylan, Mariah Carey

resources.name: SoundExchange
resources.description: Non-profit that collects digital performance royalties for sound recordings (not compositions). Covers satellite radio (SiriusXM), internet radio (Pandora non-interactive), and other non-interactive digital streams.
resources.cost: Free to register.
highlights: Collects royalties ASCAP/BMI do not cover
Pays featured artists (45%), labels (50%), and session musicians (5%)
Register even if not getting digital radio play — collects back-royalties
Does NOT cover Spotify/Apple Music interactive streams

resources.name: The MLC (Mechanical Licensing Collective)
resources.description: Non-profit created by the Music Modernization Act. Administers blanket mechanical licenses for streaming services and distributes mechanical royalties to songwriters and publishers in the US.
resources.cost: Free. Fully funded by streaming services (Spotify, Apple Music, Amazon, etc.).
highlights: Collects mechanical royalties from all major streaming platforms
Search their Missing Member Lookup for unclaimed royalties

resources.name: Songtrust
resources.description: Global publishing administrator that registers your songs with 65+ collection societies across 240 countries and collects your publishing royalties. You retain 100% copyright ownership.
resources.cost: One-time $100 setup fee per songwriter. 15% commission on performance royalties; 20% on mechanical/non-performance royalties (as of January 1, 2025).
highlights: No delivery obligations or advance requirements
~150K streams to break even on setup fee
Mechanical royalty fee increased to 20% as of Jan 2025

resources.name: Ari's Take
resources.description: Comprehensive music business blog and podcast by Ari Herstand, author of "How to Make It in the New Music Business." Covers royalties, collaboration, sync licensing, touring, and career strategy.
resources.cost: Blog and podcast: Free. Ari's Take Academy courses: Paid (varies).
highlights: Praised by Forbes as "The poster child of DIY music"
Covers collaboration, splits, PROs, and sync in depth

resources.name: DIY Musician (CD Baby Blog)
resources.description: Long-running blog and podcast by CD Baby with hundreds of actionable articles on music promotion, releasing music, royalties, and career development for independent musicians.
resources.cost: Free (blog, podcast, and newsletter).
highlights: One of the most respected indie music resources
Covers release strategies, analytics, and promotion
DIY Musician Podcast for audio learners

resources.name: Bandzoogle Blog
resources.description: Advice, inspiration, and practical resources for independent musicians. Covers marketing, website design, merchandise, revenue diversification, and music career strategies.
resources.cost: Free (blog).
highlights: Practical, actionable advice for indie artists
Covers merch, marketing, and website strategy

resources.name: Soundfly
resources.description: Online music school with free and premium courses across production, songwriting, theory, and music business. Free courses include royalty collection, home recording, and touring guides. Premium subscription (Friend of the Fly) and mentored Soundfly Live courses available.
resources.cost: Many free courses available. Friend of the Fly subscription: $39/mo or $312/year for all-access premium content. Mentored Soundfly Live courses at varied price points.
highlights: Free courses on royalties, recording, and touring
Flypaper blog with additional free articles
Mentored Soundfly Live courses with expert feedback

resources.name: Hypebot
resources.description: Daily music industry news, insights, and analysis read by 30,000+ professionals. Covers music tech, artist marketing, live music, and industry trends with a focus on independent artists.
resources.cost: Free.
highlights: Strong coverage of music tech and AI in music

resources.name: Ari's Take Academy
resources.description: Paid course platform from Ari Herstand covering royalty registration, sync licensing, touring, and release strategy. Includes community access, live Q&As, and peer feedback.
resources.cost: Paid courses (pricing varies by course).
highlights: Step-by-step courses on royalties, sync, and touring
Community of musicians and industry professionals
Students often collaborate with each other

resources.name: Splice — Skills & Blog
resources.description: Free tutorials and articles on music production, sampling, and creative workflows. Skills platform offers in-depth production courses for subscribers.
resources.cost: Blog: Free. Skills tutorials included with Splice subscription ($12.99/mo Instrument, $19.99/mo Creator, or higher).

resources.name: Pibox
resources.description: Audio review and collaboration platform purpose-built for music production workflows. Pin feedback directly to specific notes in a track for organized async collaboration. Used by major media teams including Sony and Universal.
resources.cost: Free plan (2GB storage). Paid tiers available (verify pricing at pibox.com).
highlights: Pin feedback directly to specific notes
Used by Sony and Universal media teams
Ideal for producers and mix engineers

resources.name: Lutefish
resources.description: Real-time online music collaboration platform debuted November 2024. Backed by Wenger Corporation (80-year-old music manufacturing company). Designed for online rehearsals and live session collaboration with low-latency performance comparable to playing in the same room, effective up to 500 miles away.
resources.cost: Verify pricing at lutefish.com.
highlights: Ideal for remote rehearsals and live sessions
Emerging platform with strong technical foundation
